articleTitle: Technical support: A valuable voice
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical support for reactive purposes (customer satisfaction) is becoming the number one technology differential. Technical support knows and understands customer needs. Technical communicators can develop quality user manuals when they team up with the technical support group. The benefits of creating a technical communications department that includes writers, trainers and technical support engineers are summarized.

articleTitle: Developing communication skills in engineering classes
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Temple University has developed a program which introduces engineering students to the importance of oral and written communication exercises which are spread across the four years of the engineering curricula. In the first year, students are made aware of the importance of becoming good writers and speakers and how this can impact on their careers. Exercises in proofreading are conducted by a consultant in introductory level classes. In the second year, typical exercises include classroom note taking and short verbal presentations based on the notes. Laboratory journals and more formal laboratory reports are also introduced. Additional laboratory report writing and a formal research paper are emphasized in the third year. An exercise in teamwork is presented in a third year course to help students in the many collaborative projects they encounter in upper level engineering projects. All fourth year students take a full year capstone senior design course which includes many written submissions and oral presentations.

articleTitle: Technical and business communication for entrepreneurs
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The historical as well as current national shifts toward an entrepreneurial based economy, and the impact of recent defense industry reductions on the technical communications necessities of Southern California are outlined. As technical professionals face the downsizing of industries which have traditionally been employers of these professionals, many are endeavoring to become technical entrepreneurs or "technipreneurs". This shift in the professional objectives of technologiests combined with the lack of a communications infrastructure, which adequately facilitates the reconstruction their technical characteristics, presents several unique communication challenges. The communications issues of this transition are examined, and a particular solution for communication infrastructures, which can be provided by IEEE and similar professional societies, is introduced.

articleTitle: When the writer isn't a technical person
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Most of the current members of the Society for Technical Communication, the largest professional society of technical communicators, began their careers in communications. In the 1970s, on the other hand, most technical communicators were technical people who had taken on writing tasks. This shift has created new opportunities for improving the technical writing product, as well as new problems for technical professionals, communications professionals, and managers to face and resolve.

articleTitle: Enhancing electrical engineering students' communication skills using online and hypertext aids
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The authors report on a five-year project to enhance electrical engineering students' communication skills. The approach entails (1) identifying the communication problems of students and recent graduates; (2) working with faculty to identify ways in which writing and speaking can be used to meet course objectives; (3) developing an Online Writing Center (hypertext applications, interactive writing exercises), and computer conferencing via electronic mail, electronic bulletin boards, and commenting software to support student writers and faculty who use writing in their courses; and (4) using formative evaluations to enhance the Online Writing Center products and services, and summative evaluations to assess the impact of the Online Writing Center program on student communication skills.

articleTitle: Collaboration: Chaos or creative opportunity
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Flexibility and self-reliance provide the technical communicator with creative opportunities in work environments that are in the midst of being restructured. Acts of collaboration across organizational boundaries (both within and without) are occurring more frequently. Using personal experience and a survey of professional communicators, the authors provide insight to successful collaboration, the personal and professional characteristics of an effective collaborator, and techniques to improve collaborative efforts.

articleTitle: The cooperative development of Linux
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Linux is a UNIX clone being developed by a cooperative of software authors. The entire source code is freely distributable, protected by the Free Software Foundation "copyleft." The cooperative development of Linux is examined in detail. Emerging group dynamics are surveyed to find how the current Linus "club" came to assemble itself. The "club" model shows how the facilities of the Internet and USENET became their virutal meeting place. Analysis of current projects shows how the participants divide themselves into groups according to their interest, and work in these interlocked circles to add to the entire effort. The "club" model serves as a model for future software development using electronic communications.

articleTitle: What do users really want from computer documentation?
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Information is typically the lowest rated component when measuring overall satisfaction of a software product. A survey is initiated to determine what aspects of documentation are frustrating or upsetting to computer users. The objective is to have customers define the problems as they perceive them. The methodology used, i.e., how the focus group approach enhanced the development of the actual questionnaire, is described. The major findings of the study that provide developers of computer documentation with insights and practical advice on how to improve the quality of the documentation they create are summarized.

articleTitle: The communicator's role in project teams
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Complex problems of government organizations and private companies are more frequently being addressed by project teams rather than by individuals. A communication specialist who is a member of a project team has the opportunity to create an expanded and satisfying role. The challenge is to recognize and demonstrate the skills that are needed by a team which has a particular style and approach to the group process.

articleTitle: Implications of a market economy for technical communications in Russia
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical communications in a market economy call for consideration of other disciplines not usually associated with the communication of technical information. The implications for technical communicators of the following topics are explored: audience analysis, public relations, crisis communications, total quality and other change programs, problem-solving, marketing communications, corporate culture, ethics and technical information, dealing with the media responsible technical communications in a global market environment demand that corporations and governments develop a partnership with their various publics.

articleTitle: Solutions for training the professional when money is tight
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: With the increase in full-featured computer programs in the workplace, the demand for computer training is growing. Information specialists and documentation designers as well as researchers in user documentation are frequently asked to help solve the training problem. Using a case study, three training options are analyzed, and one approach to solving the training problem is described.

articleTitle: Women in technical and scientific fields: Results of a national survey
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A national survey of women employed by organizations involved with science and technology was conducted. The object of the survey was to determine the status of women and the types of problems they were encountering in what has traditionally been a male-dominated work force. The survey examined the environment in which women work, the relationship between women's personal lives and their work, and women's interpersonal communication styles. Some results parallel those of other surveys; other results run counter to those expected. Length of time in the workplace, salary, role and position in the workplace appear to be variables that determine women's attitudes toward and perceptives of the workplace.

articleTitle: The Professional Activities Council for Engineers (PACE)
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical societies provide a variety of ways for engineers to keep up their technical skills, including journals, conferences, and videotapes. However, an engineer's job and promotion prospects are increasingly enhanced or limited by his or her professional qualifications. PACE can help engineers at all phases of their careers. The functions of the PACE committees and some of their activities are described.

articleTitle: Electronic communication in a university campus
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The communication channels inside the university campus are changing due to the implementation of newly developed electronic technologies. The electronic communication technology which provides the function to link computers as a network enables users to exchange electronic mail, log in to remote computers, and transfer files. Preliminary results from a network user survey at the National Chiao Tung University (NCTU), Taiwan are presented. The survey results including types and frequency of network use, the nature of electronic communication, and problems which users have faced.

articleTitle: New frontiers for engineering communication: Evolution of communication vehicles
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Aspects of communication vehicles and the various types of progress that have been made over the years are examined. Six aspects of communications are discussed: communication vehicles for teaching and learning; forums for communication; vehicles for search-and-retrieval of information; richness of the communication media set; vehicles for and location of communication; and the idea of linearity in communication.

articleTitle: Successful collaborative communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The authors attempt to communicate the common features of successful collaborations, and a framework for creating and maintaining environments that nurture teamwork, and to provide readers with an understanding of the functions of collaboration, and a checklist for monitoring their own collaborative relationships.

articleTitle: Understanding statistics as a tool for interpreting research
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A basis for understanding statistics and how they are used to represent and clarify research results is established. Emphasis is placed both on how statistics should be selected, based on the type of data and their distribution, and on how the results should be interpreted.

articleTitle: How audience analysis keeps engineers customer-focused
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical communication has long advocated the importance of the customer. When technical communication instructors train engineering students to focus on audiences' needs, backgrounds, abilities, and interests before designing a document or giving a presentation, instructors are emphasizing the customer. Thus, the audience analysis skill taught in the communication classroom helps engineers to prepare for the highly competitive, restructed workplace.

articleTitle: Video production and technical education
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Video in technical education ranges from recording live presentations to scripted lecture-demonstration and documentaries. Differences in approach and production values depend on the level of funding and anticipated revenues in light of the needs and expectations of the audience. Videos intended to motivate and persuade should use appropriate television techniques to get the audience's attention. For strictly informational programs, such as a technical presentation by an expert for a small audience, it may be sufficient to use minimal production values in recording a live presentation. In this case, the responsibility for the quality of the presentation would shift from the media producer to the presenter who develops the delivery and supporting graphics.

articleTitle: Electronic automation as an alternative to learning computer tasks
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Test subjects performed a mail merge using an integrated software product, Microsoft Works for Windows. Those who learned about the task from automated online help were slightly less successful in completing the task than were subjects who used an online tutorial, or than those who used only printed and online information. The automated help subjects also had comparatively negative evaluations of that help system.

articleTitle: Around the world in 80 days: Typesetting Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic, and Thai
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Many of the documents which technical editors create are translated into other languages. Usually, the information is sent to a translation service. In preparing the publications to describe the IBM Core Interchange fonts, the author had the opportunity to work with many languages and alphabets. The author seeks to increase awareness of other cultures and appreciation of foreign languages as she worked with them to create publications.

articleTitle: Directions for computer-mediated scholarship
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Current practices of computer-mediated scholarship (CMS) are analyzed, and directions for establishing CMS systems are identified. Experiences with established, disciplinary-specific CMS systems show that systems-oriented approaches to building systems for scholarship can be successful in providing a comprehensive set of features to meet the needs of scholars. The use and potential for tools-oriented approaches to CMS show that computer-mediated communication forums and network information retrieval tools can provide many needs of scholars, including searching for sources, communicating with colleagues, analyzing source materials, disseminating research, and preparing instruction.

articleTitle: Balancing visual and verbal modes of presenting information: Diagnostic tools for making effective choices
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical communicators can balance the verbal polish of their documents with refined visuals. The authors describe how to diagnose problems with information access, representation of physical concepts, and design of graphics.

articleTitle: Internationally speaking... [technical messages to international audiences]
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The expansion of the international marketplace is posing greater communication challenges. Successful business negotiations will depend upon the skills that business professionals develop to ensure that their technical messages are undamaged in translation and easily understood by their foreign audiences. Step-by-step procedures for technical professionals to follow in planning, developing, and delivering technical messages to international audiences are presented.

articleTitle: Communicating with nontechnical audiences: How much do they know?
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The importance of approaching an audience as a rhetorical consideration of the intended reader's community and its cultural contexts for writing is explored. An approach is presented to audience analysis that examines the nontechnical reader's community culture using three questions: How does this reader's community value my subject? What writing conventions operate in this reader's community? How much background knowledge is a member of this community likely to have? The author describes how a technical writer can choose an appeal based on values shared with the intended reader, and then present shared and new information in ways that accommodate the reader's needs for understanding unfamiliar technical subjects.

articleTitle: Collecting and incorporating feedback from customers: The usefulness of telephone surveys
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Some of the obstacles to collecting telephone customer feedback are examined, and a collection method is proposed that puts a less-than-expected burden on customers while, at the same time, maximizes the usefulness of the information which it is possible to obtain.

articleTitle: Skimmers - How to reach our new audience
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The authors discuss techniques to immediately attract the readers' interest to convince them that the content is worth reading. This can be accomplished by using design and writing techniques that attract skimmers, e.g., sidebars, descriptive headers, drop quotes, dedicated margins to showcase product applications, and graphics that tell a story through brief but telling captions.

articleTitle: Hype, hypertext, and reality: What the research tells us about hypertext
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The issues surrounding hypertext are discussed, and conceptual and theoretical issues are identified to guide further hypertext research. Practical guidelines for developing hypertext products are provided.

articleTitle: A model for establishing a risk communication committee in your organization
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Several writer-editors at Los Alamos National Laboratory saw a need for better communication about the risk that attends many of the activities at the Laboratory. They developed the goals of educating themselves, educating their fellow writer-editors, and improving support for the technical staff in the area of risk communication. To educate themselves, each member of the committee read a book on risk communication, prepared a book review, and presented the review to the other members of the group. To educate fellow writer-editors, they produced tip sheets - short, educational papers, each on a single aspect of risk communication. Topics for tip sheets include the definition of risk communication, overcoming barriers to communication, outrage factors, and making risk comparisons.

articleTitle: Computer supported cooperative work systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The requirements which information systems must meet to be effective in the 1990s are determined, and the limitations of present day information systems are discussed. The advantages of object-oriented databases and artificial intelligence techniques are explored as viable methodologies for meeting these requirements.

articleTitle: Uses Of Language In Collaborative Design Teams
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'

articleTitle: Collaborative writing on the job: Secrets your writing teachers never taught you
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Academic communication courses cannot continue to ignore the collaborative nature of real-world professional communication. With a little imagination, course assignments can be redesigned so that students no longer work in isolation and their writing is evaluated based on its effect on the target audience rather than on its "artistic" qualities.

articleTitle: OOW, it's object-oriented writing
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The author describes how a new concept, object-oriented writing (OOW), aids in reusing more information as well as helping provide easier-to-use information for customers. The advantages of OOW over traditional documentation approaches are outlined.

articleTitle: Hypertext technology in information design
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The initial stages in an examination of how hypertext technology can facilitate effective use of text and language in an industrial design project are described. Specifically, the effects of using hypertext both for exploring one's own design ideas in an online design notebook, and for exploring other people's design ideas in such a notebook (a situation that might come up in collaborative work) are compared. In the first phase, twelve participants completed two types of text-based activities under two conditions, i.e., once using hard-copy notes they had created and maintained themselves, and once using hard-copy notes created by someone else. Analysis of the resulting data points to a significant difference between participants' success, in terms of both accuracy and speed, in finding factual information in their own reference material versus finding factual information in reference material compiled by someone else. These results provide baseline data for the planned second stage of the study.

articleTitle: Technical communications practices and the use of information technologies as reported by Dutch and U.S. aerospace engineers
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: As part of Phase 4 of the NASA/DoD Aerospace Knowledge Diffusion Research Project, two studies were conducted that investigated the technical communications practices of Dutch and US aerospace engineers and scientists. A self-administered questionnaire was distributed. Responses are presented of the Dutch and US participants to selected questions about four of the seven project objectives: determining the importance of technical communications to aerospace engineering professionals; investigating the production of technical communications; examining the use and importance of computer and information technology; and exploring the use of electronic networks.

articleTitle: Creating shared understandings in software design
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Effective product design is predicated upon good communication between designers and clients. One possible framework for how designers might better understand a client's needs in design situations is presented. A particular software designer-client interaction is then explored in the light of the framework earlier presented.

articleTitle: Structuring document libraries for the 90's
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: There are dozens of documentation choices for virtually every planning decision. One must consider not only printed documentation, but a huge variety of online and multimedia documents as well. The authors raise the question of how responsible managers can maintain control of documentation planning and make successful tradeoffs about the appropriate support for each product and audience segment? A decision-making process that can begin early in the product development cycle, when planning decisions can be most cost-effective is presented.

articleTitle: Science fiction for technical communicators
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: An overview of science fiction, and how it relates to the field of technical communications is presented. Several works that focus on the process of communication are examined, and suggestions for further reading are presented.

articleTitle: A standard-based approach to text and hypertext mutual conversion and interchange
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Hypertext interchange and bidirectional conversion between text and hypertext are largely considered two different applications. In the authors' research, a system (SGML-MUCH) for importing and exporting SGML documents into and from a collaborative hypermedia system - MUCH (Many Using and Creating Hypermedia) system - is developed. The SGML-MUCH system is able to support both hypertext interchange and text-hypertext bidirectional conversion. The SGML-MUCH system is developed following the SHyD model, which uses international standards SGML and HyTime as intermediate formats. An SGML DTD based on a widely accepted hypertext reference model- the Dexter model, is defined to represent both text and hypertext documents. Text and hypertext documents in different formats can be imported into the MUCH system by going through the SGML representation.

articleTitle: Use of satellite technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Using satellite technology as a delivery method for education of a nontraditional nature has emerged in the last ten years and will continue into the mid-nineties. Current usages are examined, future use is forecast. The focus is on the IEEE experience and how it is meeting the needs of lifelong learning of the engineer.

articleTitle: Structure and form: Strengthening selling documents
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Using both logical and rhetorical techniques, as well as page layout, a technical writer-editor can communicate an idea to an array of audiences without sacrificing the integrity of the science. As government and industrial budgets continue to decrease, marketing documents will play an increasingly important role in obtaining funding. Audiences will have to be convinced that only one proposal out of many is worth funding.

articleTitle: Electronic bulletin boards alleviate time zones, increasing efficiency
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Electronic bulletin boards are quickly becoming an efficient means of transferring information throughout much of the world without time zone constraint. With an ever increasing amount of transcontinental development and documentation taking place, the BBS provides a forum and exchange medium for conveniently delivering information fast and without mistake. Some of the benefits realized in one high-technology business by utilizing a BBS for the collection and retrieval of information from many wide-spread sources are discussed.

articleTitle: How to improve communication with co-workers and subject matter experts
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: To produce a top quality product, technical communicators need to use informal communication channels in addition to those of the formal superior/subordinate hierarchy. Before they can be used, these channels need to be established and maintained. Four skills needed by information workers are defined, the one most often neglected by technical writers is identified, and that skill is defined in detail.

articleTitle: Using International English to prepare technical text for translation
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The International Communication Committee at Los Alamos National Laboratory has been working to develop a set of guidelines for writing technical and scientific documents in International English, that is, English for those whose native language is not English. Guidelines have been applied to preparing English technical text for subsequent translation into Russian. It is shown how International English can profitably be used for preparing high-quality text intended for translation.

articleTitle: The technical communications group: Adding value to an organization
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Whether an organization uses technical communicators as a permanent part of its organization or hires them on a per project basis, depends on the organization's culture, flexibility, and real and perceived costs. As technology continues to advance, technical communication demands are prompting organizations to recognize technical communicators as valuable internal resources whose capabilities extend beyond writing. Using professional communication skills and technical knowledge, a permanent Technical Communications Group functions as a vital link to an organization's customers and employees.

articleTitle: Channeling: A contextual approach to internal and external communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Channel is defined as "the vehicle or medium through which signals are sent. In practice, those vehicles are largely presented as text-based, messages planned in terms of contexts of audience and purpose, but ultimately organized as formats. It is argued that people are the primary channels, and that relationship-building, particularly in environments prompting linkages and/or experiencing stress, is a critical component of communicative competence.

articleTitle: International Communication And Its Role In International Business
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'

articleTitle: IEEE business meeting experiment with video teleconferencing
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The authors report on IEEE's first, major business meeting experiment utilizing video teleconferencing facilities in cooperation with BellSouth Telecommunications, Inc. The experiment utilized six, geographically-separate BellSouth sites (Atlanta, Birmingham, Charlotte, Nashville, New Orleans,and Orlando) having different teleconferencing facilities connected via T1-service. BellSouth's facilities were used to conduct the first meeting of 1993 of the Region 3 Executive Committee. A video tape of the meeting is archived in the Electrical Engineering History Center at Rutgers University.

articleTitle: Instructional design for training: A case study on educating computer users in complex tasks
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The development and implementation of a training program for users of a database accounting system in an R&D laboratory are discussed. The goal of the training program is to instruct these users, account administrators, in complex tasks, such as selecting the right accounting reports for the purposes out of over 120 options or customizing their report data and displays. Usability tests of prior instructions showed that the instructions did not help these users take advantage of database capabilities to perform complex tasks. To help users adapt their system to their complex tasks, this training program will employ cases drawn from actual problems with accounting tasks in the laboratory. Instruction will focus on the match between users' actual task goals and methods and various program capabilities, i.e., strategies for choosing the best of many possible methods, strategies for accessing the information users need and for evaluating choices, and error management.

articleTitle: Access methods for online information: A cost/benefit approach to users' choices
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Two studies that suggest the existence of varied and complex factors determining users' choices of access methods when seeking information in an online environment are reported. One of these factors is the perceived cost and benefit of using a particular access method. A cost/benefits analysis of user choices reveals that, in many cases, aversion to risk and to cognitive load affects certain user choices more than criteria of efficiency. To improve the retrievability of online information, technical communicators and tool designers need to focus on users' perceptions of the cost and benefits involved in their interactions with the tool for displaying online information, as well as with the information itself.

articleTitle: Editors, "Good English," and international readers
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The author question whether native English-speaking editors, faced with a letter in English that uses a clearly non-English structure, would change that structure in the process of turning the letter into "good English," or whether nonnative readers prefer that a letter in English be structured to reflect their own cultural expectations. Some of their findings seem to contradict recent research about sensitivity to cultural contexts.

articleTitle: The wizard of cause
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Error messages are usually the least-looked at, least paid attention to part of a software product. The importance of error messages is described. Twelve steps to make error messages more usable are suggested.

articleTitle: The neglect of writing in technical writing
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: In its fascination with equipment, the profession of technical writing is neglecting its main reason for existence, i.e., writing skills. Some tips on improving cohesion, structure, emphasis, smoothness, conciseness, and user-friendliness are given.

articleTitle: Experience transfer in Statoil
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Future growth in the oil industry will depend on learning from past experience and developing new ways of thinking and doing business. Statoil believes in involving the various parts and levels of the organization to master experience transfer. A method, named ERGODESIGN, has been developed to manage experience transfer in projects were multiple oil and engineering companies participate. The aim is to ensure that experience with technical equipment and design solutions is brought forward and employed in new platform design. A summary of ERGODESIGN's steps is presented by relating them to a specific case.

articleTitle: Secrets of the great communicators
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: In an age of education via electronics and conversation via computer, it is possible to forget the psychological and emotional bases of effective communication, believing that a system upgrade will perfect the message when, in fact, neither the hardware nor the software is the problem. The author reports on three secrets of communication: bridging the gulf; seeing the gold; and hanging around.

articleTitle: Computer-aided teaching of thermoelectrical power plant operation
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A computer aided system (SADCOM: Sistema de Apoyo Didactico Computarizado) to teach power plant principles of operation to new plant operators is described. SADCOM usex text, graphics, colors and animation to illustrate the basic processes of a power plant. The presentations are controlled by the instructor who explains how the different systems, equipment and processes work. SADCOM teaches the following topics: tube and instrumentation diagrams, operation procedures, failure analysis, and generation unit thermal balances where mass, pressures and temperatures can be modified to see how they affect the efficiency of the unit.

articleTitle: Retraining industrial employees for a career in programming
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The author describes how one American corporation (International Business Machines Corp.) took a group of its employees from varying and diverse backgrounds and re-educated them to become computer programmers. The generalities of the program are discussed. These include how the program was administered, what was the length of the program, and what were the restrictions of the program. The specific educational plan that each student was expected to undergo is reported. The bulk of the courses were computer science courses and each course is briefly described.

articleTitle: Three ways to enliven a deadly presentation to a nontechnical audience
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A "dry" or "technical" subject can be made exciting to a nontechnical audience by avoiding some common mistakes in preparation: (1) a weak start with a noncommittal "pseudo-message"; (2) overuse of abstract ideas without exemplification; and (3) visuals that just list facts or numbers instead of bringing them to life by symbolic means. Having exciting material will also greatly improved your delivery, because it naturally invites enthusiasm and confidence.

articleTitle: Getting the most out of your professional communications: A total quality approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A strategy, called a Communications Assessment, to help organizations make sure that both their technical and business written communications are consistent with each other and with corporate goals is described. The Assessment consists of interviews of key staff, evaluations of written material, and a report of the findings and recommendations. The result is a management tool that can be used as part of an internal system for continuous improvement and quality control.

articleTitle: Information Mapping on the Macintosh
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Information Mapping is a system for hierarchical spatial arrangement and organization of text to enhance readability. The process has been applied to a wide variety of documents. It enables one to present information by function, get to the point quickly, write for the reader, address the reader's need to scan, and present information in modular units. A general explanation of the Information Mapping format is given. Specific styles in Word, PageMaker, and QuarkXPress that facilitate using mapping are discussed. Styles can free writers from dealing with the format mechanics of mapping.

articleTitle: Information mapping the PCS constitution and bylaws
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Readers generally use documentation when they need answers to questions. They must be able to find the answers to these questions easily. The author describes how information mapping addresses these concerns, using the PCS Constitution and Bylaws rewrite as an example. Structured writing, more specifically, information mapping is discussed as a tool for analyzing and presenting information. The author describes: what information mapping is, emphasizing it as a method of analysis rather than a format; how it is used; and the process of information mapping the PCS Constitution and Bylaws.

articleTitle: Using a procedures database to support project-specific procedures based on a master process
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A new information mapping approach permits a procedures system database to support project-specific procedures based upon a master process. With this approach the generic steps in a procedures system database are project-specific when viewed by users. This approach is implemented by modifying commercially available procedures database software (DocuStructure). In addition to describing the information mapping approach, it is shown how the database structures have been modified to support a master process.

articleTitle: Risk analysis communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Risk assessment is based on scientific information that is often highly uncertain and speculative. Scientific representation of probability has suffered a serious loss of credibility. The acceptability of any given risk can change based on new information or on the interdependence of one risky activity on another. Risk acceptability must be determined not only one on the basis of technological expertise and statistical validity, but also in consideration of such social and ethical issues as the protection of individual rights, the equity of risk-to-benefit distribution, the legitimacy of risk assessment and risk management processes, and most importantly awareness for and respect of the public's perception of risk.

articleTitle: Curriculum for technical communication in the computer industry
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Within the field of technical communication, a prominent specialization is in the area of computers. As recent graduates from technical communications programs, the authors found that their experiences as technical writers in the computer industry varied from that of their education and internships. They surveyed graduates from various technical communications programs who graduated within the last five years and who work in the Silicon Valley. It was found that there were key areas in which their education and internship experience varied from that of their first job.

articleTitle: The nontechnical audience: A vanished species?
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The author examines the concept of the nontechnical audience. How can that audience be defined? What is the relationship of that audience to the information that is being delivered by such technical means as hypertext and videodisc? Why are we interested in this audience, if it even exists anymore? The author explores: 1) the modern definition of a nontechnical audience; 2) if that audience truly exists in today's environment; and 3) what the merging of technical and nontechnical fields makes possible in terms of communication for the future.

articleTitle: Developing a master process for the Office of Nuclear Safety
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The Master Process for operations of the Office of Nuclear Safety of the United States Department of Energy was developed as the unifying model for the complex processes and process interfaces necessary for efficient and effective performance of the Office's mission. It portrays Office functions from a systems perspective by focusing on the Office's customers, products, and work flow, instead of hierarchically by functions and divisions. This systems-based approach provides a more accurate picture of those processes which must occur at all levels of performance organization, process, and performer. The Office's Master Process includes five principal parts: strategic planning; project team operation; conduct of assessments; annual report; and self-assessment.

articleTitle: Disarming NIMBY with the facts: Field notes on explaining controversial technologies for concerned audiences
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A case study of the technical communications strategy we devised for a Florida company is given. In proposing a hazardous waste treatment facility, the firm came face-to-face with the Not In My Backyard (NIMBY) syndrome. The company was further challenged by an organized campaign from an environmentalist special interest group with a reputation for strident and disruptive tactics. The linchpin in the company's strategy for defusing the growing controversy was to lead the facts, and to present them objectively in published form. The goal was to bring forward the scientific and social underpinnings of the technology proposed for the facility. At the same time, standard modes of persuasive communication were viewed as self-serving and therefore suspect. The solution was to create informative publications modeled on science journalism.

articleTitle: Effective training techniques: Oral versus written
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Most companies and educators find it necessary to provide training before new equipment can be used effectively. Because of widespread use of computers in writing classrooms, the question often arises as to what is the most effective way to help users become proficient with the equipment. Data from an experiment testing effectiveness of oral versus written training in the use of a word processor indicate no significant difference between the two conditions. Analysis also indicates no correlation between the number of requests for help from teaching assistants and the number of measurement tasks completed.

articleTitle: Designing for dual delivery: On-line and paper a hypertext solution
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Document design concepts and their role in the development of software documentation for dual delivery. The basis for information transmission through the following three domains is examined: (1) creative thinking as a metacognitive process; (2) specific aids to information processing; and (3) cognitive theories of visual processing. Document design guidelines are provided for the printed page and small screen displays. A model of a basic hypertext document for overall effectiveness as a dual delivery document is evaluated.

articleTitle: Quality metrics for ISO 9000 documents
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: ISO 9000 is a suite of generic quality standards adopted by the EC as a condition of purchase. Firms who wish to sell to the EC will have to be registered as ISO 9000 compliant. Most manufacturing firms who aspire to compliance have far too little procedural documentation, and what they have is far too complicated ambiguous, and unreadable to meet the standard. The objective is to make quality procedures more readable and unambiguous, more maintainable, and more accessible to registars and employees.

articleTitle: Revitalizing professional communications: The Internet challenge
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: New and potential Internet users are introduced to useful network tools and resources. The focus is on how the Internet continues to revitalize professional communications. Emphasis is on clearing access hurdles, the advantages of specialized indexing services, and the use of applications software that fosters user-friendly interactive searching and expeditions file transfers. Underscored are basic search and retrieval strategies, alternative routes to similar information, techniques for successfully applying the full-range of TCP/IP protocols, and timesaving navigational shortcuts.

articleTitle: Paper what? [electronic paper]
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The advantages of electronic paper or what is called raster technology are discussed. Rasters capture the engineering drawing in a format that a personal computer (PC) can use. Raster files can then be shipped across the continent or an office building via computer networks, stored on diskettes or laser storage systems, retrieved simultaneously by hundreds of reviewers, annotated electronically, and then transmitted back to the design organization. Additional benefits accrue from the fact that tedious paper scanning is eliminated, delay in handling and mailing is avoided, rooms of flat file storage cabinets are replaced by a single laser juke box, and in general, the need for paper is reduced. Equipped with a raster system, an engineer can conduct the searching, retrieving, and mailing of the drawings without having to move away from the PC. In the case presented, the DoD CALS standard is used in a raster drawing system for reviewing the design of Space Station Freedom.

articleTitle: IEEE United States Activities Board-An Overview
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The author describes the formation of the USAB within the context of IEEE organization. The USAB goals and activities are outlined, career enhancement and employment assistance activities are described, together with national and state government activities.

articleTitle: The evolution of a technical writing course
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The development of an in-house writing course are discussed. The course was developed primarily for engineers and geologists and is divided into four segments: (1) technical reporting process; (2) report components; (3) applications; and (4) conventions and constructions. "Technical reporting process" includes a discussion of audience analysis; technical exposition; technical description, narration, and argumentation; organizing information; technical writing style; and writing and revising.

articleTitle: Information design: A human factors approach to a new typography
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: By maximizing the typographic potential of a design, information designers create documents that attract readers' attention, motivate readers to act on information, and allow readers to efficiently locate and understand information. Adopting a human factors approach to typography allows the professional communicator to adapt to the needs of users and the challenging requirements of emerging delivery media.

articleTitle: Empty pathways: Faculty use of computer mediated communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The use of electronic mail and other forms of computer mediated communication among faculty in engineering and technology is discussed. Through the interviews and case studies, the authors examine characteristics of faculty who are active users of comptuer mediated communication (CMC), as well as those who do not use the communication technology. Possible barriers to a more widespread use of this medium for instruction and professional development are examined, and remedies are suggested.

articleTitle: A new era in international technical communication: American-Russian collaboration
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Models of the Soviet-style information society and the Western-style information society are presented, the effects of centralized governmental control of information on Russian technical communication practices are discussed. The effects of political control on technical communications are then used to interpret the results of a survey of Russian and US aerospace engineers and scientists concerning the time devoted to technical communication, their collaborative writing practices and their attitudes toward collaboration, the kinds of technical documents they produce and use, their views regarding the appropriate content for an undergraduate technical communication course, and their use of computer technology. The implications of these findings for future collaboration between Russia and US engineers and scientists are examined.

articleTitle: Technical Policy Council
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The Technical Policy Council, one of five IEEE-USA councils, is responsible for interpreting and influencing US technical policies. The primary function of these councils is to affect legislation for the benefit of all Americans from the rational viewpoint of electrical engineers. To influence federal legislation and policy, USAB's five councils deal with specific areas of concern. Technology Policy Council provides "...objective technical advice to legislative and executive policy makers concerning proposed laws and regulations involving electrotechnology... 'and "...also supplies interpretations of new technologies and promotes national technology policies that enhance US, competitiveness.".

articleTitle: Cross-site writing and shared responsibilities: A team effort
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Sharing writing responsibilities for a set of manuals between two distinct company sites poses unique challenges. In the authors' experience, the situation requires clear communication using electronic technology; mutually understood, accepted, and followed agreements; and dedication to teamwork. These result in timely completed manuals, as well as in camaraderie and synergy among members of the team.

articleTitle: University minority engineering programs
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The agenda for a university minority program is examined. The purposes of the program are to recruit minority students into the engineering/science field, conduct a pre-college program for junior high students, and provide support for minority engineering students currently enrolled in the university. The focus will be on how a minority engineering program functions in a university setting. Programs such as the minority engineering have the potential of contributing significantly to the retention and eventual graduation of future engineers. It is hoped that this type of program designed to assist in the recruiting and motivating of minority students can, in the future, serve as a model to support all incoming freshman engineering/science students.

articleTitle: "New" audiences: The role of technological innovation in audience definition
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: It is argued that the traditional demographic approach to audience analysis is too narrow. It is suggested that, under conditions of rapid technological change, technical writers must expand their analytical horizon to include the underlying assumptions and contingent factors which shape both technological innovation and audiences.

articleTitle: Accent training for new arrivals
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The accent with which English is spoken is not homogeneous. This variation in accent is sometimes a source of inefficient communication for newcomers to a particular country. Even with a very good knowledge of English, accent variations can cause confusion, socially and professionally. The importance of accent training and to present a training scheme is emphasized.

articleTitle: Video teleconferencing and the integration of effective communications systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: A state-of-the-industry informational report on the history of video teleconferencing including its origin, current status, and future prospects is presented. With the recent ratification of international standards regarding the coding, exchange, and transmission of the video and audio signals betwen systems, the videoconferencing industry is ready for major expansion over the next decade.

articleTitle: Answers to questions about questions-and-answers
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The use of questions in classical rhetoric is noted, and possible advantages and disadvantages of using a pure question and answer approach in technical writing today are discussed. In theory, it should help both readers (who are looking for answers) and writers (for whom it could provide discipline). But there also negatives - primarily its potential for misuse in the hands of an unscrupulous writer. The authors recommend further testing, noting some facets that should receive particular attention.

articleTitle: Team writing
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: IBM Transaction Processing Facility (TPF) information development (ID) has implemented concept of team writing. Each writer is responsible for several publications and several line items. As a publication "owner", the writer is responsible for the organization, format, contents, and schedule. As an ID line-item "owner", the writer updates all the publications in the TPF library that relate to the specific line item. The updates are done with the approval of the publication "owner". To make this process work successfully, writers must see themselves as members of several teams - the information development department and the line-item teams. The team also consists of TPF developers, testers, service support, and market support personnel. The organization of the library, contents, and timing, are all driven by the needs of the customer. Team writing is a dynamic concept that puts the decision making with the writing team.

articleTitle: Strategies for preparing and teaching a course on technical and business communication to a foreign-language audience
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Technical communicators are in demand because professionals in other countries want to learn about the techniques used in document production and information processing. Teaching a course to a foreign language audience demands careful and thoughtful preparation, a knowledge of the culture of the host country, skill in speaking through a translator, the ability to be flexible and adjust readily to unexpected conditions, and the willingness to research and understand the audience's needs and expectations.

articleTitle: User interface design for a CD-ROM product
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The design of the graphical user interface for the Resseller Resource CD is discussed. The interface is designed to facilitate the effective use of a wide range of functions and various information types available in the product. A total of five different interfaces are provided to assist the user in locating and processing needed information. Using Open Windows environment such as buttons, pull-down menus and pop-up windows, as well as a build-in help facility, online documentation, SearchTool and Multiviewer windows, users can easily and quickly locate needed information from their own desktop. Some of the lessons learned during the development and early implementation of the Reseller Resource CD are summarized.

articleTitle: Balancing the "me, myself, and I" in technical communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: In our communication we are often confused or deceived by our self-reinforced perspective. It is important to establish, reinforce, and utilize contacts with the outside world to balance our natural self-centered point of view. Examples are drawn from areas of life that are different from the typical technical communication experiences. This is to encourage an open examination of the processes by which we operate in our professional and personal lives and to minimize the habit of thinking, "I already know how to do that.".

articleTitle: The technical document production process at the Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action Project
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: The technical document production process at the US Department of Energy's (DOE's) Uranium Mill Tailings Remedial Action (UMTRA) Project is described. Jacobs Engineering Group Inc. (JEG) is responsible for providing the DOE with high-quality technical and management support services and documentation of technical and administrative activities performed on the UMTRA Project.

articleTitle: Technical writer, technology writer: Using the trade media to build recognition for your organization and extend your professional skills
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
abstract: Professional communicators have the skills and knowledge to write authoritative trade articles about organization technology and/or business environment. Suggestions for selecting a target publication, winning the go-ahead from a senior collaborator, and working with the collaborator to develop the article are given.

articleTitle: Proceedings of IEEE International Professional Communication Conference (IPCC '93)
publicationTitle: Proceedings Professional Communication Conference The New Face of Technical Communication: People, Processes, Products'
